notes:
Check these:
1. Heligoland (570, 571, 585, 830): I made these places because your guidance names Heligoland as a place. But stations.json has a heligoland id (seen 1880, 1885m, 1887m), so remap them if you want consistency. The outlying stations are handled differently: Malmo (836, 837) and Stevns (1223) went to their ids even though some rows fall outside their seen years. 377 'Farö' is Fårö in Sweden (the duck name is Swedish), not the Faroes.
2. Teesmouth: plain 'Teesmouth' (1261, 72 obs) is mixed. Split it by year: 1880 rows → teesmouth-1880; 1879 rows (and 1510 'the Teesmouth') may be tees-lv; other years are the Redcar land observer. 1262 'Teesmouth (Redcar)' (1881-82) is mapped to teesmouth-1880 although it isn't listed in those years. 1260 (1886) may be tees-lv or south-gare.
3. Spurn: plain 'Spurn' (1179, 388 obs), 'the Spurn' and 1887 '_Spurn_' are mapped to spurn-point. Some rows may be the light-vessel or the peninsula generally. 1184 'Spurn t..' has lost its type word.
4. Happisburgh light versus light-vessel: I used the type garble and the context (on deck, rigging = LV; u.u./u.n./t.n. = L.H.). The least certain are 554, 557 and 562.
5. Pattern assumed for the OCR garbles: 1883-84 'u.u., u.H., u.n., u.a., u.x., u.z., t.u., t.x.' = L.H. and 't.v./u.v./t.y.' = L.V. In 1886, 'Lu./L.u./La' = L.H. and 'Lv./LvV./Lyv.' = L.V. Where a station has no light-vessel (Coquet, Cromer, Farne, Hanois, Whitby, Hunstanton), I read L.V. as the lighthouse.
6. Farne: plain 'Farn' / 'Farne Islands' are mapped to inner-farne (the list prints 'Farn Islands' for it). 'Farns', 'two Farn Island lighthouses', 'Farn Island stations' and 814 'Longstone lighthouses' are mapped to both inner-farne and longstone.
7. Goodwins: the collective Goodwin names are mapped to the four vessels (north-sand-head-lv, south-sand-head-lv, east-goodwin-lv, gull-lv), following 'the four lightships on the Goodwin Sands'. Check that including Gull is right for every year.
8. Pure guesses to check against the page: 1029 'Resin L.v.' (Swin?), 307 'Dowsing u.v.' (Outer or Inner?), 1249 'TE L.H.' (Tees Breakwater?), 1474 'seettie', 1530 '‘= mouth', 1059 'Rush' (probably the word 'rush', not a place), 160 'Breakwater'.
9. Great Cotes rows (505-507) are mapped to great-cotes, which is only listed in 1880. Group names like 'East Coast stations' are coded as places, not expanded to station ids.
10. Places I identified myself: 117 Beasby = Beesby, 191 Buxby = Buxey Sand, 1343 Whitley Sands, 872/1229 Stour (Kentish or Essex), 1502 'the Park' = Grainsby Park. 118: the report says 'Beccles (Norfolk)' but Beccles is in Suffolk.
